text:
maya: Hey finance/eng — saw a weird spike on NexCorp's embedding bill this morning, ~3x expected for March. Not an obvious usage pattern change on their side. Can someone check if this is a metering duplication? :eyes:
liam: I'll take a first look at the ingestion logs. Any customer sample IDs or request_ids?
maya: Added a CSV in the ticket with a couple request_ids and timestamps. Pattern looks like identical embed hashes repeated ~2-3x within 10s windows.
asif: Could be SDK-level retries that didn't dedupe on our side. We had a vendor SDK update last week that changed retry headers.
liam: grabbing logs now. quick grep shows same request_id but different event_ids, and our ingest shows multiple upstream events. snippet: ```sql
SELECT request_id, count(*) FROM embedding_events WHERE request_id IN ('r123', 'r124') GROUP BY request_id;
-- returns 3 for r123, expected 1
```
kevin: FYI billing pipeline dedup should be keyed on (customer_id, request_id, model, vector_hash). If request_id is colliding or missing we fall back to vector_hash dedupe which sometimes fails for truncated hashes.
maya: Is this an immediate billing exposure? Customer flagged invoice is already in pending review. Need estimate to refund if duplication confirmed.
liam: I see vendor header `X-Retry-Reason: idempotency-timeout` on the duplicate events. The SDK started adding a new header `x-sdk-retry-id` last week. Looks like our parser ignored it; we were still expecting `idempotency_key`. So we treated retries as new requests.
asif: Ok that explains duplications. Fix path: 1) quick patch to parser to accept `x-sdk-retry-id` as idempotency key; 2) run dedupe backfill for affected customer/day; 3) billing credit for duplicates.
maya: Can you estimate number of duplicated billable tokens & amount? Need numbers for accounting.
liam: Running aggregation now. Preliminary: NexCorp Mar 12 00:00-06:00 window shows ~1.2M duplicate embed tokens (~$120). Will confirm.
asif: I'll open a backfill job ticket. We should mark events with source SDK version so we can avoid over-deduping older ones. Also need to patch ingestion schema to record `x-sdk-retry-id`.
kevin: For backfill, recommend: 1) identify duplicates by (customer, request_id) where `x-sdk-retry-id` present; 2) generate ledger adjustments with memo "dedupe-backfill sdk-retries"; 3) dry-run on a subset.
maya: Please put the refund estimate and ledger entries in the ticket. We need finance approval before issuing credits.
jordan-bot: @maya @liam Backfill job created: BF-2027-914, dry-run scheduled. CC finance.
liam: Patch ready in branch `ingest/fix-sdk-retry-id`. Will deploy canary to staging, then prod after validation.
asif: I started a quick dry-run query: ```sql
WITH dup AS (
  SELECT customer_id, request_id, count(*) as cnt
  FROM embedding_events
  WHERE event_time >= '2027-03-12'::date
  GROUP BY customer_id, request_id
  HAVING cnt > 1
)
SELECT sum( (cnt - 1) * avg_tokens_per_event ) FROM dup JOIN event_stats USING (customer_id, request_id);
```
kevin: Once we have the exact token count, finance can approve a one-time credit. Also suggest we add a metric to billing dashboards for "dedupe-rate by SDK-version".
maya: Thanks all. Please add the final numbers to ticket BF-2027-914 and ping me when dry-run completes. I'll hold the invoice adjustment until we confirm. :+1:
liam: Dry-run done — matches earlier estimate: 1,203,400 duplicate tokens, approx $118.50 credit. Uploaded CSV of affected request_ids to ticket.
asif: Deployed parser patch. Ingestion now records `x-sdk-retry-id` and will dedupe incoming events with that key.
jordan-bot: Backfill job BF-2027-914 completed dry-run. Awaiting manual approval to run ledger adjustments.
maya: Approved the credit amount. Kevin please proceed with ledger entries and notify the customer.
kevin: Will do, creating ledger adjustments now and drafting customer note.
maya: Nice catch. Also looping in account manager for NexCorp. Let's add postmortem note on the vendor SDK change + our missing parser acceptance.
liam: I'll create a short RFC for an ingestion compatibility test to catch these header changes earlier.
asif: Also recommended: auto-alert if per-customer dedupe rate > 0.5% in a 1h window.
maya: Closing loop here — thanks everyone. "
